Working notes — ticket routing

Request routing appears based on request type, size, and region, not sender/department or subject phrasing (“asking twice”, “second attempt”, “form bounced”, “scanned”, “regional office”).

Options:
A = standard queue
B = priority desk
C = regional office

Confirmed valid:
- REQ-2405: large shipment, north region → C accepted.

Confirmed invalid:
- C rejected for: small shipment north; small shipment south; large invoice south; large invoice east; small invoice east; large refund? (not tested C); small refund east.
- B rejected for: large refund south; large shipment east.

So far, C works only for large shipments from the north. All other tested C attempts failed. B failed for the two tested cases. A has not been tested.

Tentative rule:
Use C only for large shipment/north. For other combinations, try A first unless future evidence supports B.

Do not rely on:
- sender/team name
- repeated-client or follow-up wording
- document format notes
- “regional office” phrasing unless matching the confirmed large shipment/north case

Next useful tests:
- A on any rejected combination, especially large refund/south and large shipment/east
- B on cases where A is invalid
- C on large refund/north or large invoice/north to see if type matters or only size/region.

Working notes — ticket routing

Routing depends on request type, size, region. Ignore sender/team, subject phrasing (“asking twice”, “second attempt”, “form bounced”, “scanned”, “regional office”).

Options: A=standard, B=priority, C=regional.

Confirmed valid:
- C: large shipment/north (REQ-2405).
- A: large refund/south (REQ-2413); small refund/east (REQ-2415). Refunds likely go to A.

Confirmed invalid:
- A: large claim/north; small claim/north; large invoice/north; small claim/east; small shipment/north. So A fails for claims, invoices, small shipment/north.
- B: large refund/south; large shipment/east.
- C: small shipment/north; small shipment/south; large invoice/south; large invoice/east; small invoice/east; small refund/east.

Tentative rule:
- Refunds: try A. Test other refunds.
- C only confirmed for large shipment/north.
- Invoices/claims: A invalid; B/C untested. Likely B or C.
- Shipments: small/north not A/C, so B likely. Large/east not B. Small/south not C.

Next tests:
- B on invoices (large north/east/south; small east) and claims (large/small north; small east).
- C on claims and large shipment/east.
- A on other refunds and remaining shipments (large east, small south).
- B on small shipment/north to confirm.

Do not rely on sender/team, repeated-client/follow-up wording, document format notes, or “regional office” phrasing unless matching confirmed large shipment/north case.

Working notes — ticket routing
Routing depends only on type, size, region. Ignore sender/team, subject wording, “regional office”, scanned/typed, urgency. Options A–D.

Confirmed:
- Refunds: A for all tested sizes/regions; large/east and large/south A accepted. Treat refunds as A.
- Claims: large/east B; small/east B; small/north C.
- Shipments: large/north C; large/south D (confirmed twice); small/east B.

Likely:
- Shipments: small/north B; small/south B.
- Invoices: large/north B; small/east A.

Invalid/anomalies:
- Claims small/south: A invalid; B/C untested. large/north: A invalid; B/C untested. large/south untested.
- Invoices large/east: A/B/C invalid; D untested. large/south: A/B/C invalid; D untested. small/south: A/B/C invalid; D untested. small/north: A/B untested; C invalid.
- Shipments large/east: B/C invalid; A untested. large/south anomaly resolved: D valid.

Corrections:
- Drop prior “large shipment/south anomaly/no valid A/B/C”; valid is D.
- Drop prior “large shipment/east likely B”; B and C rejected; test A.
- Small claim/north now known C, not just likely.

Next tests:
Shipments: large/east A.
Invoices: large/east D; large/south D; small/north A/B; small/south D.
Claims: small/south B/C; large/north B/C; large/south A/B/C/D.
